lesson_title: A Sheep, a Duck and a Rooster
hook_text: The first passengers to fly in a hot-air balloon were not people. They were a sheep, a duck and a rooster.
clip_script: France, 1783. A huge cloth-and-paper balloon, painted blue and gold, swells with hot air. Under it hangs a basket with a sheep, a duck and a rooster. Up it goes, in front of the king and a cheering crowd, and lands safely about eight minutes later. Then come people, then giant airships shaped like cigars, then propeller planes, then jets. Today, a jumbo jet carries hundreds of passengers across the world in a single day.
visual_style: Whiteboard sky with a hot-air balloon and three animals, a cigar-shaped airship, a helicopter and a big jet, drawn in a rising line from bottom left to top right.
mood: Light and wonder-filled, rising like a balloon.
pacing: Gentle float for the balloon, steady glide for the airship, then a roaring fast finish for the jets.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and look up next time you hear an aeroplane overhead.
